## Why this unit matters

Trace one browser request through Gateway, Order, Product and User. Learn trace/span context, collection, storage and modern instrumentation.

The same shop remains the anchor: Product owns catalogue information, User owns customer information, and Order coordinates checkout. Read each chapter in order to see which new requirement motivates the next design decision.

## Lessons

1. **[Tracing Concepts](tracing-foundations.qmd)**
2. **[Sleuth and Zipkin](sleuth-zipkin.qmd)**
3. **[Trace Transport and Persistence](trace-transport-storage.qmd)**

## Learning objective

After this unit, describe the dependency or operational problem **before** naming a framework; draw the relevant call/event path; state the failure mode and trade-off; and explain how the concept applies to a small TypeScript or NestJS service.

## Mathematical Abstraction

A trace is a graph of causally related spans.

$$
T=(S,E_{\rm parent}),\qquad E_{\rm parent}\subseteq S\times S
$$

$S$ is a set of spans and $E_{\rm parent}$ their parent-child relations; asynchronous links can require additional relationships.
